note: Expectations written by hand from REQ-lifecycle; host-model semantics only, not runtime evidence.

traces.note: duplicate callbacks do not allocate a generation; the generation allocator is global per epoch
events before a valid INIT are NOT_READY; INIT repeat compares epoch/config/catalog only
three respawns; stale callbacks of old entities change nothing; stop of an own terminal lease is OK without effects
lease pairs by leaseId, then subscriptions, binding, state, tombstone; tombstone expires at now >= expiresAtMs
live reconnect = full cleanup of the old generation, then a new one with FULL_RESYNC_REQUIRED; requestSeq restarts per generation
rejected requests consume a rate attempt and leave no effects; own busy device is DEVICE_BUSY
replay returns the current cached state (never a revived ACTIVE); evicted replay is STALE_REQUEST
capacity at priority 11 precedes the limiter; a forged burst spends the window; rate entries leave with live state
a WORLD device stays in the registry after a user's disconnect and stays limited to its access list
TTL '<' stays ACTIVE, '=' and '>' expire; a clock step back revokes once and latches until ROTATE_EPOCH
rotation revokes by leaseId, then re-generates live players in playerId order; anomaly wins over a malformed payload
a full tombstone set evicts the oldest record instead of failing
terminal records are bounded by count and TTL; an exact replay may still hit its own cache entry
an expiry during sweep may evict a higher terminal leaseId; the sweep must not trip over it (codex #861)
